overview: Two cross-references (1930, 1932): a committee considered rationalizing or merging Japan's Cement Federation companies, and a later telegram described cement conditions as unsatisfactory despite the industry's generally sound reputation; underlying telegrams filed elsewhere.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomatic officer in Japan and sender of the referenced telegrams; precise position is not stated in these documents

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram no. 219 on rationalization of the cement industry
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects researchers to telegram no. 219 concerning proposals to rationalize and consolidate Japan’s cement industry.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Neville's telegram on a Bureau committee considering rationalizing or merging Cement Federation companies.

subfiles.title: Attached excerpt on Cement Federation rationalization
subfiles.about: This fragment reports a Bureau committee’s discussion of rationalizing the Cement Federation and merging cement companies.
subfiles.summary: Attached excerpt repeats that a Bureau committee discussed rationalizing the Cement Federation, including a possible company merger.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram no. 107 on conditions in the Japanese cement industry
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects researchers to a telegram reporting contradictory assessments of the Japanese cement industry’s condition.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 107 describing unsatisfactory conditions in Japan's cement industry despite its generally sound reputation.

interest: Tracks 1930-32 Japanese cement industry rationalization plans and reported unsatisfactory conditions despite the industry's sound reputation.
